messages:
lena: Hi team 11 Lena here, starting on runtime today. I tried building from source and hit linker errors and a ptxas complaint. Any fast onboarding checklist?

lena: Build env: Ubuntu 22.04, driver 510.47, CUDA 11.7 installed in /usr/local/cuda-11.7. CMake configure succeeded but link fails: 
```
/usr/bin/ld: undefined reference to `cuDeviceGet'
```

lena: I exported CUDA_HOME and LD_LIBRARY_PATH to /usr/local/cuda-11.7/lib64 already.

paige: welcome! short checklist: 1) clean build dir (remove CMakeCache), 2) ensure CMake picks up nvcc (`-DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER=/usr/local/cuda-11.7/bin/nvcc`), 3) check final link line for -lcudart or -lcuda.

dmitri: undefined reference -> missing cudart or driver lib at link time. run `cmake --build build --verbose` and inspect the link command. If CUDA was found via new CMake config, you might need `target_link_libraries(... PRIVATE CUDA::cudart)` in the CMakeLists.

lena: I inspected link and it lacked -lcudart. After forcing CUDA::cudart the link passes in container, but locally I hit: 
```
ptxas fatal : Value 'sm_86' is not recognized for option '--gpu-name'
```

paige: that means the toolkit's ptxas doesn't know that arch string. Check `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` or any cached CUDA_ARCHS.

dmitri: also confirm `nvcc --version` and `which ptxas` match the CUDA toolkit you expect. Mixed toolkits cause that error. For local dev, we recommend `docker run --gpus all -it --rm -v $PWD:/src redwood/dev-runtime:cuda11.7` which has matching nvcc/ptxas.

lena: removing old CMake cache and setting `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86` fixed the ptxas error. Using the docker image was quicker for initial tests. Pushing a tiny onboarding PR with the commands and the docker fallback.

paige: awesome, thanks for documenting that. ping if you want someone to quick-review the PR.

infra-bot: FYI: infra ticket #4982 reminders: some VMs need /usr/local/cuda symlink to be present for CI scripts.

lena: thanks all, really helpful :heart:
